name: KeyRotationSchedule
purpose: Drives rotation of data-encryption keys on a fixed cadence with overlap window, and blocks new writes with a key past its cutover.
api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Protocol

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KeyRotationSchedule:
    key_alias: str
    cadence: timedelta
    overlap: timedelta
    next_rotation_at: datetime

class KeyRotator(Protocol):
    def schedule(self, sched: KeyRotationSchedule) -> None: ...
    def rotate_now(self, key_alias: str) -> str: ...
    def active_key(self, key_alias: str, at: datetime) -> str: ...
invariants: A new key version MUST be produced on or before next_rotation_at; missing a rotation SHALL raise an alert to the compliance channel.
overlap MUST be > 0 so decryption of records written with the prior version NEVER fails during cutover.
active_key() MUST return exactly one current key per alias at any instant; ties or gaps CANNOT occur.
Keys past cadence + overlap MUST be marked decrypt-only; new writes with such keys SHALL be rejected.
Rotation events MUST emit a TamperEvidentAuditLog entry capturing old and new key versions.
extension_contract: KMS providers implement a RotationAdapter with .create_version(alias) and .set_primary(alias, version). Target applications register schedules at startup; custom post-rotation steps are added via a rotation hook that runs inside the rotation transaction.
consumption_example:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

sched = KeyRotationSchedule(
    key_alias='alias/pii-field',
    cadence=timedelta(days=90),
    overlap=timedelta(days=7),
    next_rotation_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=90),
)
rotator.schedule(sched)
kid = rotator.active_key('alias/pii-field', datetime.now(timezone.utc))

sources.locator: Requirement 3.7.4 — cryptographic key changes at defined cryptoperiod
SC-12 Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management

why_essential: Rotation done via quarterly runbooks silently lapses; a scheduled primitive turns cadence into code and makes missed rotations a failing build signal rather than an audit finding.
alternatives_considered: Manual rotation via ops playbook — depends on humans and misses under load.
Cloud-managed auto-rotation only — covers CMKs but not application-scoped DEKs or HMAC keys.
Single long-lived key with periodic audit — leaves a long blast radius on compromise.
